blocks.content: The core constitutes about 16 percent of the Earth's volume but accounts for nearly 33 percent of its total mass due to its extraordinarily high density.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The core is the innermost layer of the Earth, extending from a depth of 2,900 km to the center at 6,371 km.
It is primarily composed of heavy metallic elements, predominantly Nickel (Ni) and Iron (Fe), earning it the acronym NIFE.
The outer core exists in a molten liquid state, while the inner core is solid despite extreme heat due to immense overburden pressure.
The Gutenberg Discontinuity marks the transition between the lower mantle and the outer core at a depth of 2,900 km.
The Lehman Discontinuity separates the liquid outer core from the solid inner core at approximately 5,150 km depth.
S-waves cannot pass through the liquid outer core, resulting in a large S-wave shadow zone between 105° and 105° from the epicenter.
Convective motion of molten iron in the liquid outer core combined with Earth's rotation drives the geodynamo effect, producing Earth's magnetic field.
P-wave velocity drops sharply at the mantle-core boundary (Gutenberg Discontinuity) before increasing again as it passes into the dense inner core.
